problem: Segment-level matchers such as SegMASt3R put all learnable capacity in a per-segment feature head followed by a parameter-free Sinkhorn solver, with no cross-segment mixing. They also match strictly pairwise, so they collapse at wide baselines where two views share few segments.
motivation: Object-level mapping, topological navigation and scene graphs need object identity across views, not pixel or keypoint matches. Wide-baseline viewpoint change is where appearance fails and intermediate views could bridge the gap, so joint reasoning over several views should help.
key_idea: Match instance segments with a learned attention head (LightGlue-style DoubleSoftmax) on frozen 3D-foundation-model features, and extend it to joint self-attention over segments from N views at once on VGGT features.
insight: Which head wins depends on the viewpoint regime. On Replica, LGv2 leads at narrow baselines (91.17 AUPRC at 0-45°) but falls 11.4 points below Sinkhorn at 135-180°, where the Joint model leads. Joint beats pairwise DPT by 4.3 AUPRC at the widest Replica bin, and on VKITTI2 extra views help only at the widest baseline (71.05 to 78.22). The temperature-clamp ablation shows that calibration of the scorer, not richer descriptors, limits SegVGGT-DPT, since clamping τ≤1 cuts false-dustbin errors by 36%.
method: Shared template: frozen backbone gives per-patch features, SAM masks are used for masked average pooling into one descriptor per segment, and a learnable projector maps descriptors to a 128-d embedding (up to 100 segments per image).

SegMASt3R+LGv2: frozen MASt3R 24-d local descriptors go through an MLP to 128-d, then 3 blocks of weight-shared self-attention, bidirectional cross-attention and an FFN. Scoring uses DoubleSoftmax (log p(j|i)+log p(i|j)), a matchability classifier and a SuperGlue-style dustbin (~800K trainable parameters).

SegVGGT-DPT: DPT-style fusion of VGGT Aggregator layers {5,11,17,23} (1x1 conv to 256 channels, Residual Convolutional Unit fusion) is applied before mask pooling, followed by the same attention stack and head as LGv2 (~10.7M trainable parameters, learned τ≤1).

SegVGGT-DPT Joint (main): per-view descriptors get learned per-view position embeddings and are concatenated into one sequence. Three joint self-attention layers (no cross-attention) refine it, and DoubleSoftmax is read off for any requested pair. It is trained with N=4 and evaluated at N in {2,4,6,8} without retraining.
Training: ScanNet++ with GT correspondences from projected 3D instance IDs. Loss is normalised NLL over GT pairs plus BCE matchability (λ=0.3). AdamW, lr 1e-4, cosine schedule, bf16, 2x RTX 5090.

Closed-loop integration: each matcher replaces the online segment localizer in RoboHop (FastSAM segments, ±8-frame window of the teach-run map, Dijkstra planner) with no retraining. The Joint model runs at N=2.

setting.model_size: Heads ~0.8M (LGv2) and ~10.7M (VGGT-DPT) trainable parameters on ~1B frozen backbones

numbers_note: The HM3D 'val' split label is the minival subset; the paper does not name a split. The N-sweep and temperature-clamp results are only in figures. Replica and VKITTI2 are custom stratified protocols, so their 'test' label is a placeholder.
results: On the HM3D IIN minival (10 episodes), the Joint variant raises SR from 50% (SegMASt3R Sinkhorn) to 70%, and LGv2 raises SPL from 45.70 to 59.14, both beating RoboHop's LightGlue baseline (40% SR, 39.87 SPL). Offline, LGv2 gains +4.85 AUPRC on Replica and +25.87 on VKITTI2 over Sinkhorn, and Joint wins the widest indoor bins.
limitations: Trained only on indoor ScanNet++, and the learned heads extrapolate poorly to extreme rotations (LGv2 is 11 AUPRC below Sinkhorn at Replica 135-180°); VGGT heads transfer poorly to VKITTI2.
Closed-loop evaluation uses only 10 minival episodes, with simulator depth and traversability, and real-world evidence is qualitative only.
Joint SPL is lower than LGv2 (49.04 vs 59.14), and seeds are not fixed, so sub-point differences between VGGT rows are unreliable.
